key_insight: Bulk Cs2AgBiI6, a long-sought lead-free iodide double perovskite, can be synthesized in phase-pure microcrystal and thin-film forms by halide exchange from Cs2AgBiBr6 when trace moisture is removed.
engineering_relevance: This establishes a practical route to stable, low-toxicity absorber materials for solar and photodetector devices, enabling experimental study of a previously inaccessible 3D iodide double perovskite.
method: Prepared phase-pure Cs2AgBiBr6 microcrystals as the precursor.
Removed trace moisture to enable complete anion exchange to Cs2AgBiI6.
Made phase-pure films by flash thermal evaporation of Cs2AgBiBr6 followed by anion exchange.
evidence_signal: The product showed broad visible absorption with a 1.70 ± 0.05 eV bandgap, near-infrared photoluminescence at 1.03 eV, long-term room-temperature stability, and photoconductivity in thin films.
watch_item: The synthesis is moisture-sensitive, so strict drying and inert handling are likely required to reproduce phase-pure Cs2AgBiI6.
paper_title: Synthesis of the Elusive Bulk Iodide Double-Perovskite Semiconductor, Cs2AgBiI6: Microcrystals and Photoconductive Films
